shape.basis: O'Dell et al. (2013, Sect. III.1 and III.3): the Main Ring's semi-axes on the sky are 44 arcsec along position angle 60 degrees and 30 arcsec across it, its pole tipped 6.5 +/- 2 degrees from the line of sight with the south-west end moving away; velocity ellipses fitted to the long-slit spectra give the Main Ring 19 +/- 2 km/s in [N II] and [S II] and 9 +/- 2 km/s in [O III], and the central region (the polar Lobes) 36 km/s in [N II], 28 km/s in [O III] and 20 km/s in He II; O'Dell, Sabbadin & Henney (2007), as restated there, find expansion of 0.65 km/s per arcsec from the star. The display's red channel is [N II] and [S II] with H-alpha, its green [O III], its blue He II; in the Main Ring, where there is no He II, the blue channel takes the [O III] speed. The Lobe's radius is that of the elongated ellipsoid through the molecular shell's polar openings in Kastner et al. (2025, Sect. IV): 2.3e17 cm at 782 pc, 19.7 arcsec.
